chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl, from his father, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said:
I said to him, 'Should a man look at the woman he intends to marry, so he looks at her hair and her beauty?' He said, 'There is no problem with that when there is no deriving pleasure.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to look at a woman's hair and beauty when intending to marry her?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of a suitor viewing a prospective bride's hair and physical features to assess compatibility, a practice rooted in the Prophet's tradition. The condition of 'not being sexually pleasured' (talladhdhun) distinguishes this permissible inspection from the general prohibition of the gaze (nazar), emphasizing intentionality over mere visual contact. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the validity of marriage contracts based on mutual attraction and suitability.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, form Abdullah Bin Al Fazl, from his father, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can the man look at the woman intending to marry her, so he looks at her hair, and her beauty?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with that when there does not happen to be deriving pleasure’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl from a man who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who wants to marry a woman; if he can look to her hairs and beauty. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is lawful if it is not with lust.’”
